change_summary: The paper has been withdrawn at the request of the editor, and its full text and PDF have been replaced by the withdrawal statement. The withdrawal is because the indoor temperature records analysed in the paper had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and the notice states that the reported results cannot be relied on. The paper's indoor results came from the indoor temperature loggers, and its headline result was a 2.1 °C lower mean daily peak indoor temperature in green-roofed flats than in the paired control flats, while it also reported that living rooms in green-roofed flats spent 41% fewer hours above 28 °C. The withdrawal touches the whole paper, including its indoor temperature findings, so those findings cannot be relied on.
evaluation: In Section 2.2, your draft sets the model's green-roof indoor cooling effect to 2.1 °C, the reduction measured in the field study by Okafor et al. [14], and the paper reported that the mean daily peak indoor temperature in green-roofed flats was 2.1 °C lower than in the paired control flats. In the Discussion, your draft says that the green-roof result scales almost directly with that 2.1 °C, and that if the value were halved, green roofs would no longer outperform reflective coatings. The paper has been withdrawn at the request of the editor, and the notice says its indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. The withdrawal touches the Section 2.2 use, because the 2.1 °C parameter is one of the paper's indoor-temperature results, and it touches the Discussion use, which rests on that same result. The impact on your draft is high, because the withdrawn result supplies your model's key parameter.
recommendation: The paper has been withdrawn at the request of the editor, and the notice says its indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. In Section 2.2, your draft sets the model's green-roof indoor cooling effect to 2.1 °C, the reduction measured in the field study by Okafor et al. [14], and the withdrawal touches that use, because the 2.1 °C parameter is one of the paper's indoor-temperature results. In the Discussion, your draft says that the green-roof result scales almost directly with that 2.1 °C reduction, and that if the value were halved, green roofs would no longer outperform reflective coatings. Because your model depends on this value, raise the withdrawal with your co-authors or supervisor before editing the text. Find a reliable replacement source for the parameter, rerun the model, and then re-check the Discussion's conclusions and remove or replace citation [14].
